key_insight: Intrinsic Fréchet means on unknown manifolds can be approximated using only local sampling and observed distances, without knowing the intrinsic geometry.
engineering_relevance: The method enables geometry-aware averaging of nonlinear data, including probability distributions represented in Wasserstein space.
method: Adaptively sample the unknown manifold and build a distance-based graph.
Approximate geodesic interpolation for iterative Fréchet mean optimization.
Extend ISOMAP metric-equivalence guarantees to Riemannian ambient spaces.
evidence_signal: Under stated assumptions, the analysis guarantees an O(1/T) expected objective gap using at most Õ(T^(4d+3)) sampled points; numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness.
watch_item: The sample bound grows steeply with intrinsic dimension d, raising scalability concerns despite the convergence guarantee.
paper_title: Computing Fréchet Means on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
